clash/two: Two programs need OpenSSL, but different versions of it. The first wants three point four. The second wants one point one.
clash/shared: Most systems keep libraries in one shared folder, like slash user slash lib. That folder has one place for OpenSSL.
clash/overwrite: Install one point one, and it replaces three point four. The second program works, and the first one breaks.
clash/want: So we want something a shared folder cannot do: every version, kept at once.
folder/own: Nix gives every build its own folder, all of them under one directory: slash nix slash store.
folder/make: The smallest way to make one is built-ins dot to file. It takes a name and some text, and writes the text into the store.
folder/read: What comes back is a store path: the store, then a hash, which is a fixed-length fingerprint, then a dash and the name you gave it.
folder/hash: The hash is always thirty two characters, in an alphabet of digits and letters with four missing: e, o, u and t.
folder/ro: Once a path is in the store, it is read-only. Nix never changes it in place.
hash/from: That hash is not random. Nix computes it from everything that went into the path.
hash/diff: Change one character of the input, and the hash comes out completely different.
hash/side: So two versions of a library get two different folders. They sit side by side, and neither one can touch the other.
hash/same: Now run the first one again. Same input, same path.
hash/skip: That gives Nix a shortcut. If the path is already in the store, the work is done. If a shared cache has it, Nix fetches it and builds nothing.
into/file: You can put files of your own in the store, too. Here is a small one.
into/insert: Inside a string, a dollar sign and braces insert a value. Insert a local path, and Nix copies that file into the store, and the string becomes the new store path.
into/where: The hash follows the contents, not where the file came from. The same file from two folders lands at one store path.
